newsitem.title: USA: Altera slips after failing to meet some high hopes.
newsitem.headline: Altera slips after failing to meet some high hopes.

text.p: Shares of Altera Corp dropped about five percent after the semiconductor company's first quarter earnings failed to meet some investors' bullish expectations, analysts said.
"They exceeded the street consensus, but didn't come in quite as strong as the whisper numbers that had been circulating before hand," said Charles Boucher, an analyst with UBS Securities.
"But overall, they had a strong quarter and the outlook was very robust," Boucher said.
Altera told analysts in a conference call Thursday morning that it expects to post sequential sales growth over the near term, analysts said.
Altera, however, dropped 2-1/2 to 46-3/4 in afternoon trading and was one of the most active Nasdaq issues.
Shares had risen as high as 50-1/8 in the past few days on the hopes that it would surpass Wall Street expectations, some analysts said.

After the market closed Wednesday, Altera posted first quarter earnings of $0.35 per diluted share on sales of $142 million, slightly higher than Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.33 a share. During the first quarter last year, Altera earned $0.33 per diluted share on sales of $137 million.
"I'm really surprised they are under such pressure. They had a great quarter and fundamentals remain strong," said Nimal Vallipuram, an analyst with Bear Stearns.
Vallipuram said there has been some concern in the market that semiconductor orders from networking companies have been slowing.
"There has been a perception, or misperception, that networking orders are weak. But I think orders are on track," Vallipuram said.
Vallipuram said he raised his 1997 earnings expectations to $1.60 a share from $1.55 a share and the 1998 estimates to $2.10 a share from $1.95 a share.

Altera was just one of several semiconductor stocks that were weak on Thursday. Semiconductor stocks have been volatile in recent days, fluctuating on any news that hinted of the sector's future strength, analysts said.

The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index fell 7.78 points or 2.77 percent to 281.01. Xilinx Inc shed 2-11/16, LSI Logic Corp lost 1 to 38-7/8, Advanced Micro Devices slipped 1-1/2 to 40 and Intel Corp 3-5/8 to 138-5/8.
